In the KRIT1 variant group, two patients (22.2%) had splice-site mutations, and the others had protein-truncating variants. (Table S1) All of the mutations were null. The CCM2 group comprised one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a missense mutation. The PDCD10 group included one patient with a nonsense mutation and one with a splice-site mutation. One patient (K3) presented with headache and neck pain. Brain and spine MRI demonstrated CCM and spinal CM. At the age of 52 years, a follow-up spine MRI revealed an increased size and prominent heterogeneous enhancement of T2 high signal intensity around the CM in the thoracic spinal cord. The neuroradiologist suggested the possibility of CM with a recent hemorrhage and tumorous condition. The surgical biopsy exhibited diffuse midline glioma, classified as WHO grade IV.
